## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Sīlavīmaṁsakajātaka* (Ja 86), translated as *A Test of Virtue*, belongs to the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional narrative framework, the Buddha related this story while residing at Jetavana about a brahmin who put his reputation for goodness to the test [SuttaCentral]. A closely related version of the introductory narrative appears in Jātaka 362, in which a protagonist resolves the question of whether moral conduct or erudition is superior, concluding that virtue (*sīla*) is indeed higher than learning (*suta*) [Readings from the Jatakas].

In discussions of Buddhist narrative literature, J. S. Speyer observes that the title *Sīlavīmaṁsa(ka)-Jātaka* represents an old class of traditional story headings derived from an action (the examination of virtue) rather than the name of the Bodhisattva or an object [Speyer 1895]. Related titles also appear in extra-canonical or regional jātaka lists [Nyanatusita 2008]. SuttaCentral records four translations across four languages [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identified no significant internal Pali text reuse or cross-language parallels meeting its similarity threshold [DharmaNexus].
